title: What is the Chandrayaan-3 mission's key scientific result?

sources.title: Chandrayaan-3 - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Chandrayaan-3 (CHUN-drə-YAHN / ˌtʃʌndrəˈjɑːn /) is the third mission in the Chandrayaan programme, a series of lunar-exploration missions developed by ISRO. The mission consists of Vikram, a lunar lander, and Pragyan, a lunar rover, as replacements for the equivalents on Chandrayaan-2, which had crashed on landing in 2019.

sources.snippet: Mar 1, 2024 · It is equipped with a Vikram lander and Pragyan rover. An in-depth review is carried out to discuss the findings of the Chandrayaan-3 mission. The goals of Chandrayaan-3's mission are: (a) to show a safe and soft landing on the surface of the Moon; (b) to showcase roving lunar rover technology; and (c) to carry out in-situ scientific research.

answer:
The sources report several scientific results from Chandrayaan-3 but do not single out one as "key." The most prominent quantitative result is that scientists from NRSC/ISRO estimated that about 2.06 tonnes of lunar epiregolith were ejected and displaced over an area of 108.4 m² around the landing site.

Other reported results include: LIBS confirmed the presence of Sulphur (S) on the lunar surface through unambiguous in-situ measurements [3]; APXS on the rover detected the presence of minor elements [3]; RAMBHA-LP measured near-surface plasma content [3]; ILSA listened to movements around the landing site [3]; and the first observations came from the ChaSTE payload onboard the Vikram Lander [3]. The mission's stated objectives were to demonstrate safe and soft landing, demonstrate rover roving, and conduct in-situ scientific experiments [4][6].
